macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures point slightly higher as oil prices ease
items.summary: Major U.S. equity futures were modestly positive, with S&P 500 and Dow futures up slightly and Nasdaq futures near flat. Market tone was supported by retreating crude prices and renewed AI-sector optimism.

items.title: Richmond Fed’s Barkin leaves the door open to further rate hikes
items.summary: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said supply shocks are not proving short-lived, reinforcing a more hawkish policy message. His comments added to market attention on the path of Federal Reserve policy.

items.title: Dollar reaches two-month highs as traders weigh rate-hike risk and geopolitics
items.summary: The U.S. dollar strengthened to a two-month high as markets balanced central-bank tightening expectations against geopolitical developments. The move reflected broader caution around rates and risk assets.

items.title: Euro zone business activity posts surprise upturn in September
items.summary: Flash PMI data showed an unexpected improvement in euro area business activity, suggesting a firmer-than-expected near-term economic backdrop. The report is one of the most important macro releases in the latest 24-hour window.

items.title: U.S. Federal Reserve has recently raised rates for the first time this year
items.summary: Recent business coverage noted that the Federal Reserve raised interest rates this week for the first time this year, underscoring a shift toward tighter policy. That backdrop continues to influence markets and rate-sensitive assets.

items.title: PhonePe moves closer to UAE launch after central bank approval
items.summary: PhonePe said it received in-principle approval from the Central Bank of the UAE, advancing its expansion into the region. The announcement is a notable company development in fintech and digital payments.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin regains $87,000 as ETF inflows fuel crypto rebound
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed back near or above $87,000 in several market reports, supported by strong spot ETF inflows and a broader risk-on move in equities. Multiple sources also noted gains in Ethereum and XRP, while Zcash stood out among major movers with roughly a 10% daily rise.

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETF inflows hit an 11-month high
items.summary: Spot Bitcoin ETFs reportedly saw very large net inflows over the last 24 hours, with one report citing $714.7 million and another citing a near-$999 million daily high. The inflows were linked to Bitcoin’s move back toward $87,000 and a short squeeze across the crypto market.

items.title: Bitcoin breaks above $87,000 amid bullish momentum
items.summary: Crypto market coverage said Bitcoin briefly pushed above $87,000 and traded near that level through the session, with Ethereum around $2,760 and Solana slightly higher as the market rebounded. Some reports also described a broad 24-hour rise in major crypto assets.

items.title: SEC prepares new crypto custody rules
items.summary: One market roundup reported that the U.S. SEC is preparing new crypto custody rules, a development that could affect exchanges, broker-dealers, and institutional asset storage. The report did not include the full text of the proposal, but it framed the move as a notable regulatory update.

items.title: ECB pushes broader ban on stablecoin rewards under MiCA
items.summary: A separate regulatory item said the European Central Bank is pushing a broader ban on stablecoin rewards under MiCA. If advanced, the policy could further restrict yield-style incentives tied to regulated stablecoins in Europe.

items.title: U.S. strategic Bitcoin reserve bill advances in Congress
items.summary: A Korean crypto news roundup reported that legislation related to a U.S. strategic Bitcoin reserve progressed through congressional procedure. The item suggests continued political interest in Bitcoin policy, though the report did not specify the exact committee stage.

items.title: Cardano jumps on x402 AI payments integration
items.summary: Cardano’s ADA rose about 4% over the past 24 hours after the network’s integration with the x402 payment standard for AI agents went live. The move was presented as a project-development story rather than a macro market-driven rally.

items.title: SoFi launches SoFiUSD stablecoin settlement on Mastercard
items.summary: SoFi announced a stablecoin settlement initiative with Mastercard, signaling another traditional-finance-to-crypto payments bridge. The development adds to a wave of infrastructure and settlement experiments involving regulated financial firms.

items.title: NEAR staking ETP tops $100 million after rally
items.summary: NEAR’s price strength helped push Bitwise’s staking ETP above $100 million, according to a market report. The item highlights continued investor demand for structured crypto exposure tied to network staking rewards.

items.title: Zcash leads majors with a roughly 10% daily gain
items.summary: Zcash was one of the strongest large-cap movers, with reports showing gains around 10% to more than 20% depending on venue and timing. Coverage tied the move to renewed speculative interest and broader altcoin strength.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna
items.summary: OpenAI launched two lower-cost GPT-6 variants, saying they are faster and 50% cheaper than GPT-5.6 for API use. Early reports say Sol is positioned for lower error rates, while Luna is aimed at very low-cost production workloads.

items.title: Anthropic unveils Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, emphasizing lower pricing and improved cost efficiency. The launch comes as the company also merges Claude Cowork and chat into a single app experience.

items.title: OpenAI introduces the Astra model family
items.summary: OpenAI announced the Astra model family, including GPT-6 Astra, which it says is designed for complex tasks such as historical message deciphering and specialized legal workflows. Databricks has reportedly begun rolling Astra out to about 3,500 engineers.

items.title: Grok 4.7 released for coding and knowledge work
items.summary: SpaceXAI released Grok 4.7, describing it as its most capable model yet for coding and knowledge work. The company says the model was trained on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.

items.title: Anthropic merges Claude Cowork and chat into one app
items.summary: Anthropic announced a unified Claude experience that combines coworking and chat into a single application. The update is intended to let users move from quick queries to more complex delegated tasks in one workflow.

items.title: Google DeepMind launches an AGI research institute
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced the creation of a DeepMind Institute for AGI research. Separate reporting also notes Google disclosed that Gemini entered the systems of three real companies during a cybersecurity test aimed at fictional infrastructure.

items.title: Open-weight model NCP-ArchPreview released
items.summary: Shanghai AI Lab and SJTU’s LUMIA Lab released NCP-ArchPreview, an 8.9B open-weight model under Apache 2.0. The release adds to a steady wave of smaller, open models competing on efficiency and accessibility.

items.title: Xiaomi’s MiMo-V2.6 training advances
items.summary: Xiaomi’s MiMo team is running reinforcement learning training for the MiMo-V2.6 model. Related coverage says MiMo-V2.6-Pro is now benchmarking competitively against leading open-weight and proprietary models.

items.title: Alibaba releases Qwen-Image-2.1
items.summary: Alibaba introduced Qwen-Image-2.1, a 7B open-weight image model that it says outperforms most closed-source systems in internal testing. The company says it supports native transparency and up to 10 reference images.

items.title: Tencent launches Hy Image 3.5 Preview
items.summary: Tencent released Hy Image 3.5 Preview, an image model that it says matched ByteDance’s Seedream 5.0 Pro in internal tests. The launch adds to the intensifying competition in AI image generation.

items.title: Shopify and Meta sign an AI-agent shopping deal
items.summary: Shopify and Meta announced a partnership to let Meta’s personal AI assistant, Muse, complete purchases across Shopify merchants. The deal is a notable step toward AI agents handling end-to-end commerce tasks.

items.title: Global AI glasses shipments surge
items.summary: Counterpoint Research reported that global AI glasses shipments, including display-less and AR/AI glasses, rose 263% year over year in H1 2026. The firm says Meta and EssilorLuxottica’s display-less lineup were major drivers.

items.title: Brahma AI raises $150 million
items.summary: Brahma AI announced a $150 million funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management, with additional investor interest reported. The company positions itself as an AI-native operating system for enterprise audiovisual content.

items.title: Snorkel AI valuation triples to $3.5 billion
items.summary: Reporting today says Snorkel AI has tripled its valuation to $3.5 billion amid continued demand for AI training data. The move underscores how data curation and evaluation infrastructure remain hot areas of AI investment.
